features.summary: FusionMultiSelect, the reference slice (D17.8): one declaration of the Syncfusion MultiSelect by its JavaScript names, each named as EJ2 names it, value, dataSource, dataBind, showPopup, hidePopup, change and filtering, each EJ2 33.1.47's public member; the payloads of change and filtering, nested in the declaration under EJ2's names; the input it is, generic over the member it binds, its value that member's own type and committed by change; and the render helpers that render it bound to a model member and name its fields. Main spreads the slice over seven files whose events, writes and calls name members by strings over ComponentRef, payload classes with setters, extensions that take the pipeline, and a Reactive extension on the vendor's builder; the redesign declares it in one file, the shape the rewrite keeps, with its value typed by the bound member, which admits null as the vendor's value holds null until a choice (M21.X1), and its data named as every framework read names it (M21.D1).

sentences.text: public Property<IEnumerable<TItem>> Items<TItem>() where TItem : class => Property<IEnumerable<TItem>>("dataSource");
internal static string Of(MemberInfo member) => member.GetCustomAttribute<JsonPropertyNameAttribute>()?.Name ?? Of(member.Name);

FusionMultiSelect<TValue> declares the EJ2 MultiSelect by its JavaScript names, TValue the type of the member it binds: value as Value, a Property<TValue> that holds null until a choice, so the bound member's type admits null (string[]?, int[]?) and Value.Set(null) clears the selection as main's SetValue(null) does; dataSource as DataSource<TItem>(); dataBind, showPopup and hidePopup as DataBind, ShowPopup and HidePopup; and change and filtering as Change and Filtering, whose payload is the listener's first argument.

Change hands FusionMultiSelect<TValue>.MultiSelectChangeEventArgs, which reads Value, the bound member's type, and IsInteracted; Filtering hands FusionMultiSelect<TValue>.FilteringEventArgs, which reads Text, writes PreventDefaultAction, and calls UpdateData with any source of a list, a response body's among them.
A FusionMultiSelect<TValue> bound to a member is an input: its Value, the member's own type, committed by Change, is what a form sends and a check reads.

field.FusionMultiSelect(build => ..) renders FusionMultiSelect<TProp>, TProp the bound member's type, under the field's id and binding name, starting at the member's value as M21.D1 writes it; field.FusionMultiSelect(items, build => ..) hands EJ2 the items the same way; and Fields<TItem>(text, value) and Fields<TItem>(text, value, groupBy) name each field as every framework read names it.

The rendered FusionMultiSelect<TProp>'s Reactive(m => m.Change, pipeline) and Reactive(m => m.Filtering, pipeline) handle its events from the plan's start, their payloads typed by the bound member; pipeline.Input(m => m.Allergies).Component<FusionMultiSelect<string[]?>>() reaches it in any block.

features.summary: The package: FusionComponent, the base of every Fusion declaration, which carries Syncfusion's vendor as data, its object at ej2_instances.0 on the element and its events heard by addEventListener and removeEventListener, so the one driver follows it as it follows an app's vendor; the writing every Fusion render helper uses for the C# values it hands EJ2 (M21.D1), by which AddReactiveFusion, a registration that only sets Newtonsoft's process-wide default to camel case on both lines, leaves; and the rules each slice's own declaration follows on the core's public surface: EJ2's names, payloads nested under EJ2's names, presence marks, data members named by JsonPropertyName, and a value of the app's own data typed by a type parameter. Main names its vendor by the string fusion, which its runtime picks a driver by.

sentences.text: public sealed override ComponentVendor Vendor => FusionVendor;
public static IServiceCollection AddReactiveFusion(this IServiceCollection services)

FusionComponent.FusionVendor is ComponentVendor.Define("fusion", objectPath: "ej2_instances.0", subscribe: "addEventListener", unsubscribe: "removeEventListener"), and each Fusion event declares its payload as the listener's first argument.

A Fusion render helper hands EJ2 the component's starting value and the items the view gives it as a JRaw of the text field.ValueJson and field.Json(options) write, so EJ2 writes them with the names and escapes the plan's own writer gives.
No Fusion door writes a Newtonsoft setting: an app's own JsonConvert calls keep the app's settings, and AddReactiveFusion leaves.

Every Fusion declaration marks optional: true on each member EJ2's TypeScript marks ?, as Kanban's ActionEventArgs marks cancel and Schedule's NavigatingEventArgs its dates, so a member EJ2 leaves out reads nothing and a required one it lacks stops the pipeline; ALIS022 checks the marks both ways.

Every Fusion declaration names each member as EJ2 names it, in Pascal case, so M11.D1 gives its JavaScript name with no name: argument, and EJ2's parameter kinds of one member are overloads of its one name; a name: argument is written only where C# refuses EJ2's name, a second member of one name and one parameter list (CS0111).

Every payload of a Fusion event, and every object a member holds or a method returns, is a class nested in its own component under the name EJ2's TypeScript gives its type, a type EJ2 leaves unnamed named for the event or member that holds it, and each data member such a class reads or writes against a member EJ2 declares carries [JsonPropertyName] with EJ2's name (X17.48); no slice nests a class another slice declares.

A value EJ2 types as a union of kinds that is the app's own data is typed by a type parameter, the bound member's type for an input and the app's choice at the member otherwise, and the vendor contract analyzer checks each type argument the views give against one type the union holds (ALIS037); a member whose type is loose and no browser fact pins (spec/probes/ej2-payloads.mjs, rerun on every vendor upgrade) is declared by no Fusion door, and an app onboards it on the core's surface (M12.N1).

meanings.meaning: A Fusion render helper gives EJ2 each C# value it writes into the component's options, its starting value and the items the view hands it, as a Newtonsoft JRaw of the text the plan's one literal writer writes (D17.13, N17.10, D7.7), under the app's System.Text.Json options and escaped as M19.D3 escapes the plan, so the data names each member as every framework read names it (D2.9); EJ2 writes a JRaw as its text (probe:fusion-ej2-builder-raw-json). The vendor builder's own DataSource(object), reached through the build callback, stays the vendor's, named by the app's own Newtonsoft settings, since EJ2 writes C# data through JsonConvert.DefaultSettings (probe:fusion-ej2-builder-newtonsoft-defaults); no Fusion door writes a Newtonsoft setting, and AddReactiveFusion, which only set that default to camel case for the whole process, leaves.

features.summary: FusionAIAssistView: one declaration of the Syncfusion AIAssistView by its JavaScript names, prompt, activeView, executePrompt, addPromptResponse, scrollToBottom and its three events, each EJ2 33.1.47's public member; the payloads nested under EJ2's interface names; a response set whole from the app's endpoint, with no stream in 1.0, and a prompt with its response added through EJ2's PromptModel; and the render helper that renders it under the developer's id. Main spreads the slice over nine files whose methods take literals alone, so no response body reaches the view, and whose CancelRequest writes a cancel EJ2 never reads; the redesign declares it in one file, the shape the rewrite keeps, its helper returning the rendered component, with a door that streams a part of a response, which the rewrite leaves.

sentences.text: public void AddPromptResponse(Arg<string> outputResponse, Arg<bool> isFinalUpdate) => Method(outputResponse, isFinalUpdate);

FusionAIAssistView declares the EJ2 AIAssistView of @syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat by its JavaScript names: prompt as Prompt, a Property<string>; activeView as ActiveView, a Property<int>; executePrompt, addPromptResponse and scrollToBottom as ExecutePrompt(prompt), AddPromptResponse and ScrollToBottom; and promptRequest, promptChanged and stopRespondingClick as PromptRequest, PromptChanged and StopRespondingClick, whose payloads are FusionAIAssistView.PromptRequestEventArgs, FusionAIAssistView.PromptChangedEventArgs and FusionAIAssistView.StopRespondingEventArgs; each EJ2 33.1.47's public member (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.d.ts:480, :538, :940, :950, :959, :728, :734, :741). Each method takes its arguments from any source, a response body's text among them, where main's take literals alone; main's SetPrompt is Set on Prompt.

FusionAIAssistView.PromptRequestEventArgs, EJ2's PromptRequestEventArgs nested under its name (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.d.ts:335-380), reads Prompt and PromptSuggestions, a string? and a string[]?, each optional as EJ2 marks it and null until set, as D17.5 reads the @default null EJ2 documents on each (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.d.ts:358, @syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.d.ts:367; M21.X905). It declares no Cancel: EJ2 sets cancel false and reads it from no listener of promptRequest (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.js:1337, :1354), so a listener that sets it true leaves the prompt sent and its response waiting (probe:ej2-aiassistview-promptrequest-cancelled; M21.X901), and a view declines a prompt by answering it with AddPromptResponse. responseToolbarItems and attachedFiles, which neither line declares, are not added. FusionAIAssistView.PromptChangedEventArgs (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.d.ts:381-413) reads Value and PreviousValue, each a string? and null until set, as D17.5 reads the @default null EJ2 documents on each (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.d.ts:387, @syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.d.ts:395; M21.X905), and declares no member for event and element, the DOM's objects; FusionAIAssistView.StopRespondingEventArgs (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.d.ts:414-440) reads Prompt and DataIndex, the prompt whose response the user stopped and its place in the view's prompts. They replace the redesign's FusionAIAssistViewPromptRequestArgs, FusionAIAssistViewPromptChangedArgs and FusionAIAssistViewStopRespondingClickArgs and main's three classes.

AddPromptResponse(outputResponse) sets the waiting prompt's whole response (M21.D901): EJ2 takes isFinalUpdate as true when it is left out (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.js:2172), renders the response once and puts the send button back (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.js:2222). It declares no isFinalUpdate, where the redesign's AddPromptResponse and main's take one: false hands EJ2 a part of a response and waits for more, a stream, and streaming is out of 1.0 (the owner's decision), carried by this whole-response door.

AddPromptResponse(Arg<FusionAIAssistView.PromptModel> outputResponse) adds a prompt with its response: EJ2 types the argument Object (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.d.ts:950), its source reads the object's prompt, response, isResponseHelpful and attachedFiles (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.js:2197-2204), and the browser lists and shows the prompt and the response the object holds (probe:ej2-aiassistview-addpromptresponse-object). FusionAIAssistView.PromptModel is EJ2's PromptModel nested under its name (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview-model.d.ts:8-47), Prompt, a string?, since EJ2 documents it null until set (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview-model.d.ts:15) and D17.5 reads it so, a prompt that reads nothing is handed as null (M21.X905), and Response as text, each named by [JsonPropertyName] (X17.48). It carries main's AddPromptResponse(prompt, response) and the redesign's AddPromptResponseModel under EJ2's one name, an overload C# accepts, so the redesign's name override leaves. The text door does not carry it: text handed with no prompt waiting lists an entry whose prompt is null (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.js:2190-2192; probe:ej2-aiassistview-addpromptresponse-text-unrequested).

Html.FusionAIAssistView(plan, elementId, build => ..) renders the view under the id the developer chose on EJ2's AIAssistViewBuilder, as both lines do, and returns the rendered component in place of main's FusionAIAssistViewBuilder<TModel> and its Reactive extension; its Reactive(a => a.PromptRequest, pipeline) handles its events from the plan's start, and pipeline.Component<FusionAIAssistView>(elementId) reaches it from any block.

meanings.meaning: An AI Assist view's response is set whole and comes from the app. The view's PromptRequest handler sends the payload's Prompt to the app's own endpoint through the HTTP pipeline, and its success scope hands AddPromptResponse the response body's whole text, which EJ2 renders once as the waiting prompt's answer, isFinalUpdate being true when it is left out (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.js:2172, :2222); its error scope answers with the view's own text, since EJ2 reads no cancel back and a prompt left unanswered keeps its stop button (probe:ej2-aiassistview-promptrequest-cancelled). Nothing streams in 1.0 (the owner's decision): no door takes isFinalUpdate, and the render helper writes enableStreaming false on EJ2's AIAssistViewBuilder after the view's build callback, an option the vendor builder has, its TypeScript does not declare, and EJ2's source reads to stream every response (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.js:2179, :2180).

defects.defect: Main's CancelRequest writes cancel true on promptRequest's payload (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionAIAssistView/Events/FusionAIAssistViewPromptRequestArgs.cs:36-39 at 623dd4a27), which EJ2 sets false and reads from no listener (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.js:1337, :1354): the prompt stays sent and listed, its response waits and the stop button shows (probe:ej2-aiassistview-promptrequest-cancelled), so a view that declines a prompt leaves the user waiting on an answer that never comes. The rewrite's FusionAIAssistView.PromptRequestEventArgs in M21.N3 declares no Cancel, so the write does not compile, and a view declines a prompt by answering it with AddPromptResponse.

Both lines declare the view's payload text and its prompt model's prompt with no null: the redesign reads promptRequest's Prompt and PromptSuggestions as ReadOnly<string> and ReadOnly<string[]>, promptChanged's Value and PreviousValue as ReadOnly<string>, and types the model's Prompt string (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionAIAssistView/FusionAIAssistView.cs:79, :82, :89, :92, :65 at 65fdf118d), and main's payload classes hold each as a string or a string[] that starts empty (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionAIAssistView/Events/FusionAIAssistViewPromptRequestArgs.cs:16, :19, Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionAIAssistView/Events/FusionAIAssistViewPromptChangedArgs.cs:9, :12 at 623dd4a27), each project compiled with nullable enabled, where EJ2 documents each member null until set (@syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview.d.ts:358, :367, :387, :395, @syncfusion/ej2-interactive-chat/src/ai-assistview/ai-assistview-model.d.ts:15). The vendor contract analyzer (N17.2) reads a member documented @default null with null added to its type (D17.5) and refuses each declaration by ALIS019; a probe that saw a value shows only that the member held one then. The rewrite reads the four payload members as string? and string[]? and types the model's Prompt string?.

sentences.text: FusionButton declares the EJ2 Button by its JavaScript names: content, iconCss and cssClass as Content, IconCss and CssClass, each a Property<string>; disabled, isPrimary and isToggle as Disabled, IsPrimary and IsToggle, each a Property<bool>; iconPosition as IconPosition, a Property<FusionButtonIconPosition>; and dataBind, click and focusIn as DataBind, Click and FocusIn; each EJ2 33.1.47's public member (@syncfusion/ej2-buttons/src/button/button.d.ts:86, :58, :79, :64, :70, :92, :51, :176, :184; @syncfusion/ej2-base/src/component.d.ts:129). EJ2's Button raises created alone (@syncfusion/ej2-buttons/src/button/button.d.ts:111), so the slice declares no event, and a click on the button is the element's own, heard through the DOM's EventTarget vendor (D17.3).

FusionButtonIconPosition is EJ2's IconPosition (@syncfusion/ej2-buttons/src/button/button.d.ts:8-25), Left, Right, Top and Bottom, under the redesign's name beside the class, since a type nested in FusionButton under EJ2's name would share its name with the IconPosition property, which C# refuses (CS0102). It carries a string enum converter, System.Text.Json's JsonStringEnumConverter<FusionButtonIconPosition> with integer values refused, so the live form writes each value by its name as EJ2's enum holds it (D7.7, M21.X801), and a value cast from a number outside the four throws where the view renders, as main's ToSyncfusion refuses it; X17.46 names JsonStringEnumConverter<FusionButtonIconPosition> alone, so the type check's reading of a converter by the names it writes is a gate 2 item.

Main's SetContent, SetCssClass, SetDisabled, SetPrimary and SetToggle each write one member and call dataBind; the rewrite writes it with Set on the member's Property and calls DataBind() where the view wants the change at once, and main's SetIcon(iconCss, position) is IconCss.Set then IconPosition.Set.

FusionDialog.BeforeOpenEventArgs reads Cancel, a Property<bool> EJ2 reads back to keep the dialog closed (@syncfusion/ej2-popups/src/dialog/dialog.d.ts:134; @syncfusion/ej2-popups/src/dialog/dialog.js:1622), and FusionDialog.BeforeCloseEventArgs reads Cancel, read back to keep it open (@syncfusion/ej2-popups/src/dialog/dialog.js:1739), and IsInteracted, a ReadOnly<bool> (@syncfusion/ej2-popups/src/dialog/dialog.d.ts:159, :163); each payload is nested under EJ2's interface name, where the redesign names them FusionDialogBeforeOpenArgs and FusionDialogBeforeCloseArgs, and declares no member for container, element, target and event, which hold the DOM's objects; maxHeight, closedBy and preventFocus, which neither line declares, are not added.

Open, Close and OverlayClick are each an Event with no payload (D17.4), since EJ2 types all three Object (@syncfusion/ej2-popups/src/dialog/dialog.d.ts:572, :596, :636), so no member ships without a probe, and overlayClick hands its listener the DOM's own click event (@syncfusion/ej2-popups/src/dialog/dialog.js:183); they replace the redesign's empty FusionDialogOpenArgs, FusionDialogCloseArgs and FusionDialogOverlayClickArgs and main's FusionDialogOpenedArgs and FusionDialogClosedArgs.

sentences.text: The declaration takes EJ2's class name, FusionUploader, Fusion and EJ2's Uploader (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.d.ts:483), the prefix keeping it apart from Syncfusion's own C# names beside it, as UploaderBuilder in Syncfusion.EJ2.Inputs (the owner, 2026-11-09: "to avoid name collision"); both lines' FusionFileUpload and its render helpers are renamed to it.

FusionUploader declares GetFilesData as a method returning the files the uploader lists, EJ2's public getFilesData, in place of the filesData both lines read, which EJ2 marks private (M21.X707); Files as the browser File of each listed file by M21.D701; ClearAll as a method; and Selected, EJ2's event before files are added, and FilesChanged, raised by the framework's component code once they are, as events whose payload is the listener's first argument; each EJ2 member named as EJ2 33.1.47 names it.

FusionUploader.SelectedEventArgs, EJ2's selected payload, reads FilesData, the files just chosen, and writes Cancel, which refuses them, as the browser hands them (probe:ej2-payload-uploader-selected); FusionUploader.FilesChangedEventArgs reads FilesData, the files the uploader lists; and FusionUploader.FileInfo, EJ2's file item, reads Name, Size, Type, Status and RawFile (probe:ej2-uploader-getfilesdata-selected, probe:ej2-uploader-getfilesdata-preloaded). A count is p.From(args.FilesData).Count(), which carries main's FilesCount (M21.X708).

A FusionUploader bound to a file member, IFormFile or a list of it on net10 and MVC 5's posted-file base or a list of it on net48 (D10.23), is an input: its Files, committed by FilesChanged, is what a form-data request sends, a file going in form data alone (D9.16), and a check reads it (M21.X710).

field.FusionUploader() and field.FusionUploader(build => ..) render the uploader under the field's id and binding name with automatic upload off, so the files go with the form; the framework's own component code raises FilesChanged once the uploader holds the chosen files, since EJ2's change follows a server upload alone.

The rendered FusionUploader's Reactive(u => u.Selected, pipeline) and Reactive(u => u.FilesChanged, pipeline) handle its events from the plan's start; pipeline.Input(m => m.CarePlanDocuments).Component<FusionUploader>() reaches it in any block (N14.4).

meanings.meaning: An Uploader's files are what its public getFilesData() lists (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.d.ts:1177): each item's rawFile is the browser's File for a file the user chose (probe:ej2-uploader-getfilesdata-selected) and text for one the app lists through the builder's files (probe:ej2-uploader-getfilesdata-preloaded), where EJ2's TypeScript types rawFile string | Blob (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.d.ts:97). FileInfo.RawFile is declared BrowserFile?, and text read as a file reads nothing (D3.3), so Files, and the form-data request that sends it, holds the files the user chose alone. FilesChanged is the framework's: its component code raises it after EJ2's selected and removing, once the list holds the change, since EJ2's change fires after a server upload or removal alone (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.js:1130, :2249), and its payload's FilesData is getFilesData()'s list.

features.oracle: Syncfusion EJ2 33.1.47's Uploader as its TypeScript declares it (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.d.ts, SelectedEventArgs and FileInfo there), its selected payload and file items as the browser hands them (probe:ej2-payload-uploader-selected, probe:ej2-uploader-getfilesdata-selected, probe:ej2-uploader-getfilesdata-preloaded), and as its source raises change (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.js), each JavaScript name read there by hand, scratchpad m21/tools/dts.py's flags taken as leads; and the browser, by the facts named and the promises where a defect has them.

defects.defect: The redesign reads the uploader's filesData, which EJ2 marks @private (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.d.ts:535-540): its declaration's FilesData (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionFileUpload/FusionFileUpload.cs:21 at 65fdf118d), which its Files and its input read, and its component code's FilesChanged payload (Alis.Reactive.Assets/components/fusion/file-upload.ts:18 at 65fdf118d); main names it as the value member (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionFileUpload/FusionFileUpload.cs:16 at 623dd4a27). The vendor contract analyzer (N17.2) refuses a member its type does not make public by ALIS016 (D17.5). The rewrite reads the same list through getFilesData(), which EJ2 declares public (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.d.ts:1177), in the declaration and in its component code.

Main's selected payload declares FilesCount and IsInteracted (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionFileUpload/Events/FusionFileUploadOnSelected.cs:12, :15 at 623dd4a27), members EJ2's selected payload does not have (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.js:1290-1300; probe:ej2-payload-uploader-selected), so a condition on the count of chosen files reads nothing and never holds. The rewrite's FusionUploader.SelectedEventArgs in M21.N22 declares neither, so such a read does not compile, and counts FilesData.

Main reads the uploader's value as text, ComponentProperty<string> over filesData (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionFileUpload/FusionFileUploadExtensions.cs:22, :29 at 623dd4a27), a list of file items (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.d.ts:540), so a comparison of it with text compiles and reads a list. The rewrite's Files in M21.N22 is ReadOnly<IReadOnlyList<BrowserFile>>, as the redesign's is.

Both lines render the Uploader over a member of any type, InputBoundField<TModel, TProp> with no constraint on TProp (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionFileUpload/FusionFileUploadHtmlExtensions.cs:27 at 623dd4a27; Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionFileUpload/FusionFileUpload.cs:102 at 65fdf118d), while the input sends files, so an uploader bound to text compiles and the endpoint binds no file into it. The rewrite's helpers in M21.N22 take a file member alone, IFormFile or a list of it on net10 and MVC 5's posted-file base or a list of it on net48, the file members D10.23 names (spec/Core/DESIGN.md:2313-2314).

Both lines render the Uploader by EJ2's Uploader(id), which binds no member, with automatic upload off and the input named by the member's path, .AutoUpload(false) and ["name"] = setup.BindingPath (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionFileUpload/FusionFileUploadHtmlExtensions.cs:34-36 at 623dd4a27; Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionFileUpload/FusionFileUpload.cs:106-110 at 65fdf118d), since a browser starts a file input with no file. A helper that drops AutoUpload(false) sends each file the moment it is chosen, EJ2's autoUpload true (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.d.ts:600-602), one that drops the name sends the file under no member, and one at another id leaves the plan's FilesChanged (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionFileUpload/FusionFileUpload.cs:37 at 65fdf118d) listening to no component, against D17.13.

promises.page: An admission's care plan document, rendered by field.FusionUploader() for a model whose CarePlan is an IFormFile, whose FilesChanged handler sets the element chosen's text to the count of the uploader's Files, and whose Save button posts the form as form data to an endpoint that echoes the file name of the CarePlan it bound; chosen starts as 0.
promises.gesture: Choose care-plan.pdf in the uploader, then click Save.
promises.outcome: chosen reads 1 at once, the network log holds no request until Save, and the echo reads care-plan.pdf.
promises.opposite: Clicking Save with no file chosen, the echo reads no file.
promises.defect: The uploader sends the file the moment it is chosen, so the network log holds a request before Save; or the input carries no name, so the echo reads no file; or it is rendered at another id, so chosen stays 0.

verdicts.reason: A string names the component's value member, which ALIS009 refuses on the public surface, and main's browser reads that name as text (gather.ts:168 at 623dd4a27); the declaration names its typed value property and the event that commits it (M7.N3).

EJ2's selected payload has no filesCount (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.d.ts:154-196; @syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.js:1290-1300; probe:ej2-payload-uploader-selected), so main's read finds nothing (M21.X708); the count of the files just chosen is p.From(args.FilesData).Count() over the payload's FilesData.
Main's payload is a C# class whose setter no view runs in the browser; a member the vendor reads back from its listener is the payload's declared Property.

EJ2's selected payload has no isInteracted (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/uploader/uploader.d.ts:154-196; probe:ej2-payload-uploader-selected), so main's read finds nothing (M21.X708); a selection is always the user's, by the file chooser or a drop.
Main's payload is a C# class whose setter no view runs in the browser; a member the vendor reads back from its listener is the payload's declared Property.

features.summary: FusionGrid: one declaration of the Syncfusion Grid by its JavaScript names, its data, paging, sorting, filtering, searching, grouping, columns, selection, editing, exports and print, each EJ2 33.1.47's public member; the payloads of its ten events; the render helper that renders it with an element id the view gives and a plan; the column field names, edit templates and edit dialog it writes; and the column rules it gives the grid from the validator. Main spreads the slice over twenty-two files whose calls name members by strings over ComponentRef, payload classes with setters, extensions that take the pipeline, a builder of its own and a Reactive extension on it; the redesign declares it in five files, the shape the rewrite keeps, with its exports awaited, its enums written as EJ2 reads them, its rows named as every framework read names them (M21.D1), and every column rule either checked by the column's editor or refused where the view renders.

sentences.text: public Property<IEnumerable<TRow>> Rows<TRow>() where TRow : class => Property<IEnumerable<TRow>>("dataSource");
public Property<IFusionGridPage<TRow>> Page<TRow>() where TRow : class => Property<IFusionGridPage<TRow>>("dataSource");
public void ShowColumn(Field key) => Method(key, Fixed("field"), name: "showColumns");
public void AddRecordAt<TRow>(Arg<TRow> data, Arg<int> index) where TRow : class => Method(data, index, name: "addRecord");
public static BrowserRule Email(string message) => new PatternRule(EmailPattern, "", message, Condition.Always);

FusionGrid declares the EJ2 Grid by its JavaScript names, each as EJ2 names it: dataSource as DataSource<TRow>(), and as Page<TRow>(), the result and count of a remote page, whose name: "dataSource" C# needs, the two having one parameter list (CS0111); its paging, sorting, filtering, searching and grouping; its columns' ShowColumns and HideColumns by field, AutoFitColumns with and without a field, ReorderColumns and GetColumnByField, returning a FusionGrid.Column; its selection; its editing, AddRecord with and without an index, UpdateRow, SetRowData, SetCellValue, EditCell, UpdateCell, SaveCell and GetBatchChanges<TRow>(), returning FusionGrid.BatchChanges<TRow>, whose AddedRecords, ChangedRecords and DeletedRecords are the app's rows where @syncfusion/ej2-grids/src/grid/base/grid.d.ts:3565 says Object (probe:ej2-grid-get-batch-changes); Refresh, RefreshHeader, OpenColumnChooser and Print; each EJ2 33.1.47's public member.

ExcelExport, CsvExport and PdfExport are declared MethodAsync, as grid.d.ts declares each to return a promise, so a step after an export runs once its file is written and a failed export stops its pipeline (D11.3, B15).

DataStateChange, ToolbarClick, RecordClick<TRow>(), RowSelected<TRow>(), ActionBegin<TRow>(), ActionComplete<TRow>(), BeginEdit<TRow>(), CellSave<TRow, TValue>(), CellSaved<TRow, TValue>() and BeforeBatchSave<TRow>() hand payloads nested in FusionGrid under EJ2's names, FusionGrid.RecordClickEventArgs<TRow>, FusionGrid.RowSelectEventArgs<TRow> and FusionGrid.BeforeBatchSaveArgs<TRow> among them, read with Read, each payload's cancel its Property<bool>, and BeforeBatchSave's BatchChanges a FusionGrid.BatchChanges<TRow> (probe:ej2-payload-grid-beforeBatchSave); every payload, and dataStateChange's action, declares name, the event's name EJ2's observer writes on each payload a listener hears (probe:ej2-payload-grid-dataStateChange, probe:ej2-payload-grid-rowSelected).

FusionGrid.SortDirection, EJ2's SortDirection, and FusionGrid.FilterOperator, named for filterByColumn's filterOperator, which EJ2 types as text, carry System.Text.Json's string enum converter, so the live form writes Ascending and contains as sortColumn's SortDirection and filterByColumn's operator take them (D7.7).

Html.FusionGrid(plan, id, rows, build => ..) renders the grid with the rows the view hands it, written by M21.D1, and FusionGridColumns.Of<TRow>().Field(r => r.Member) names a column's field as every framework read names it.
The rendered grid's Reactive(g => g.RecordClick<TRow>(), pipeline) and its other events handle the grid from the plan's start, and pipeline.Component<FusionGrid>(id) reaches it from any block.

FusionGridValidation.From<TRow>(rules).Field(r => r.Member) gives a column the validator's rules its editor checks, each in the validator's own form, and refuses where the view renders a rule the editor cannot check that is not the server's (M21.X203).
FusionGridEditTemplates.Select, DateInput and DialogForm write a column's editor and an edit dialog, each select opening at the row's value.

features.oracle: Syncfusion EJ2 33.1.47's Grid as its TypeScript declares it (@syncfusion/ej2-grids/src/grid/base/grid.d.ts, its event payloads in src/grid/base/interface.d.ts, SortDirection in src/grid/base/enum.d.ts, BatchChanges in src/grid/base/type.d.ts, the toolbar's ClickEventArgs in @syncfusion/ej2-navigations, a column's rules as @syncfusion/ej2-inputs' FormValidator reads them), each JavaScript name read there by the lead and checked by scratchpad m21/tools/dts.py, whose redesign members named by a JavaScript name not their own (showColumns, hideColumns, autoFitColumns, addRecord) and generic payloads were read by hand; the Syncfusion.EJ2.AspNet.Core 33.1.47 builder as spec/probes/AspNetCoreBinding/FusionProbes.cs renders it; and the browser, by spec/probes/ej2-payloads.mjs's Grid facts (probe:ej2-payload-grid-rowSelected and the six beside it, probe:ej2-grid-get-batch-changes, probe:ej2-payload-grid-beforeBatchSave) and the promises.

defects.defect: Main calls the grid's excelExport, csvExport and pdfExport as plain calls (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridToolingExtensions.cs:38-59 at 623dd4a27) and the redesign declares them Method() (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGrid.cs:207-213 at 65fdf118d), while each returns a promise (@syncfusion/ej2-grids/src/grid/base/grid.d.ts:3849, :3859, :3870): the step after an export runs before its file is written, and a failed export goes unseen. The rewrite declares them MethodAsync (D11.3, B15).

A rule a grid column's editor cannot check is dropped where the view renders with nothing said: a rule under a condition (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridValidation.cs:96 at 623dd4a27, :112 at 65fdf118d); a rule EJ2's column validator has no key for, as GreaterThan or a comparison with another member (:104-138 at 623dd4a27, :120-144 at 65fdf118d); and one of two patterns on one column (:119-121 at 623dd4a27, where the second replaces the first, and :132 at 65fdf118d, which keeps the first). The column saves a value its validator refuses, and only the server's answer says so. The rewrite refuses it where the view renders: "'{member}' has a rule the grid column's editor cannot check ({rule}); check it on the server with ServerOnly(), or give the column a rule its editor checks."

Main's select editors open at their first option: the column template's Select and the edit dialog's Select write no selected option (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridEditTemplates.cs:88-95 and :146-151 at 623dd4a27), so a row whose status is Discharged opens its editor at Admitted, and saving it unchanged writes Admitted. The redesign selects the row's value (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridEditTemplates.cs:111, :121-122, :192 at 65fdf118d), which the rewrite keeps.

Main gives an email or url column EJ2's own email and url rules (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridValidation.cs:108-110 at 623dd4a27), whose patterns need a dotted domain (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/form-validator/form-validator.js:29-32), so an inline edit refuses rose@ward and http://intranet/residents, which the server's EmailAddress and Url accept. The rewrite writes the validator's own patterns as the column's regex, as the redesign does (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Validation/BrowserRule.cs:62, :69 at 65fdf118d).

A column bound to a member that carries [JsonPropertyName("room")] shows empty cells for rows handed over with the view: a column's field names the member by System.Text.Json (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridColumns.cs:37 at 65fdf118d) while EJ2 writes the builder's DataSource through Newtonsoft as roomNumber (probe:fusion-ej2-builder-newtonsoft-defaults). The rewrite's render helper hands the rows by M21.D1 (probe:fusion-ej2-builder-raw-json).

The redesign's FusionGridSortDirection and FusionGridTextFilterOperator carry no string converter (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGrid.cs:270, :280 at 65fdf118d), and a JsonStringEnumMemberName holds only under one, so in the live form (D7.7) sortColumn receives 0 where SortDirection is 'Ascending' | 'Descending' (@syncfusion/ej2-grids/src/grid/base/enum.d.ts:40). The vendor contract analyzer's type check (N17.2) refuses an enum against the vendor's literal union by ALIS037 (X17.46), and the rewrite's enums carry System.Text.Json's string enum converter. Main writes both as text by hand (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridQueryExtensions.cs:153-164 at 623dd4a27).

promises.page: A residents grid whose Export to Excel button sets the status to Exporting, runs ExcelExport, then sets the status to Exported.
promises.outcome: The Excel file's download starts while the status reads Exporting, and the status reads Exported after it.
promises.opposite: Before the click, no download starts and the status reads Ready.
promises.defect: The status reads Exported before the download starts, since the export's promise is dropped.

promises.page: A residents grid whose Export to CSV button sets the status to Exporting, runs CsvExport, then sets the status to Exported.
promises.outcome: The CSV file's download starts while the status reads Exporting, and the status reads Exported after it.
promises.opposite: Before the click, no download starts and the status reads Ready.
promises.defect: The status reads Exported before the download starts, since the export's promise is dropped.

promises.page: A residents grid whose Export to PDF button sets the status to Exporting, runs PdfExport, then sets the status to Exported.
promises.outcome: The PDF file's download starts while the status reads Exporting, and the status reads Exported after it.
promises.opposite: Before the click, no download starts and the status reads Ready.
promises.defect: The status reads Exported before the download starts, since the export's promise is dropped.

promises.page: A ward grid whose Beds column takes FusionGridValidation's rules for a validator whose Beds rule is GreaterThan(0) When(r => r.IsOpen).
promises.outcome: The page is refused where the view renders with M21.X203's message, naming Beds and its conditional rule.
promises.opposite: The same rule with no condition renders, and editing Beds to 0 shows its message under the cell.
promises.defect: The conditional rule is dropped, the page renders, and a row saves 0 beds with no message until the server answers.

promises.page: A ward grid whose Beds column takes FusionGridValidation's rules for a validator whose Beds rule is GreaterThan(0).
promises.outcome: The page is refused where the view renders with M21.X203's message, naming Beds and GreaterThan.
promises.opposite: With GreaterThanOrEqualTo(1) the page renders, and editing Beds to 0 shows its message under the cell.
promises.defect: GreaterThan has no column key and is dropped, so a row saves 0 beds with no message until the server answers.

promises.page: A contacts grid whose Email column takes FusionGridValidation's rules for a validator whose Email rules are Matches("^[a-z.]+@") and Matches("@care\\.org$").
promises.outcome: The page is refused where the view renders with M21.X203's message, naming Email and its second pattern.
promises.opposite: With Matches("@care\\.org$") alone the page renders, and editing Email to rose@ward.com shows its message under the cell.
promises.defect: One pattern is dropped and the page renders, so a row saves an address only the dropped pattern refuses (rose@ward.com, or Rose@care.org) with no message until the server answers.

promises.page: A residents grid whose Status column edits with FusionGridEditTemplates.Select over Admitted, Discharged and On leave, and a row whose status is Discharged.
promises.gesture: Double-click the Discharged row's Status cell.
promises.outcome: The editor's select shows Discharged.
promises.opposite: On a row whose status is On leave, the select shows On leave.
promises.defect: The select opens at its first option, Admitted, and saving the row unchanged writes Admitted.

promises.page: A residents grid that edits in a dialog written by FusionGridEditTemplates.DialogForm with a Status select over Admitted, Discharged and On leave, and a row whose status is Discharged.
promises.gesture: Select the Discharged row and click Edit.
promises.outcome: The dialog's Status select shows Discharged.
promises.opposite: On a row whose status is On leave, the dialog's select shows On leave.
promises.defect: The dialog's select opens at Admitted, and saving the dialog unchanged writes Admitted.

promises.page: A contacts grid whose Email column takes FusionGridValidation's rules for a validator whose Email rule is EmailAddress().
promises.gesture: Double-click a row's Email cell, type rose@ward and press Enter.
promises.outcome: The row saves rose@ward, as the server's EmailAddress accepts it.
promises.opposite: Typing rose and pressing Enter shows the email message under the cell.
promises.defect: EJ2's own email pattern needs a dotted domain, so rose@ward shows the email message and the row does not save.

promises.page: A links grid whose Address column takes FusionGridValidation's rules for a validator whose Address rule is Url().
promises.gesture: Double-click a row's Address cell, type http://intranet/residents and press Enter.
promises.outcome: The row saves http://intranet/residents, as the server's Url accepts it.
promises.opposite: Typing intranet/residents and pressing Enter shows the url message under the cell.
promises.defect: EJ2's own url pattern needs a dotted domain, so http://intranet/residents shows the url message and the row does not save.

promises.page: A beds grid rendered by Html.FusionGrid(plan, "beds", rows, build => ..) with the rows East 1 and East 2, of a bed class whose room member carries [JsonPropertyName("room")], and a Room column whose field is FusionGridColumns.Of<Bed>().Field(b => b.RoomNumber).
promises.outcome: The Room column shows East 1 and East 2.
promises.opposite: A Ward column bound to a member with no JsonPropertyName shows the ward of each row too.
promises.defect: EJ2 writes the handed rows through Newtonsoft as roomNumber while the column names room, so the Room column shows two empty cells.

features.summary: FusionInPlaceEditor: one declaration of the Syncfusion InPlaceEditor by its JavaScript names, each named as EJ2 names it, value, disabled, enableEditMode, save and its element's classList, each EJ2 33.1.47's public member; the payloads of its seven events, nested in the declaration under EJ2's names, each as the browser hands it; the input it is, generic over the member it binds, so its value and change's value and previousValue read the member's own type, the kind each editor type hands (M21.X404); and the render helper that renders it bound to a model member. Main spreads the slice over twelve files whose calls name members by strings over ComponentRef, payload classes with setters, extensions that take the pipeline and a Reactive extension on the vendor's builder; the redesign declares it in one file, the shape the rewrite keeps, with no call of a private member (M21.X402), a starting value read with no compile (M21.X403) and its value typed by the bound member.

sentences.text: public sealed class FusionInPlaceEditor : FusionComponent, IInputComponent
public ReadOnly<TResponse> Data<TResponse>() where TResponse : class => ReadOnly<TResponse>();

FusionInPlaceEditor<TValue> is generic over the member it binds: its render helper renders it with the member's type, so Value, a Property<TValue> whose type argument admits null, as D17.5 reads the @default null EJ2 documents (@syncfusion/ej2-inplace-editor/src/inplace-editor/base/inplace-editor.d.ts:184-187), the input M7.N3 builds from it, and change's Value and PreviousValue read and write the member's own type, as main reads the value by the member the field registers (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditorExtensions.cs:111-115 at 623dd4a27): text for a Text editor, a number for Numeric, a DateTime for Date, a DateTime[] of its two days for DateRange and a list of the items' values for MultiSelect, the kind EJ2 hands each (probe:ej2-inplaceeditor-change-Text, probe:ej2-inplaceeditor-change-Numeric, probe:ej2-inplaceeditor-change-Date, probe:ej2-inplaceeditor-change-DateRange, probe:ej2-inplaceeditor-change-MultiSelect); pipeline.Input(m => m.Member) reads it as a BoundInput of the same type (N14.4).

FusionInPlaceEditor<TValue> declares the EJ2 InPlaceEditor by its JavaScript names: value as Value; disabled as Disabled and enableEditMode as EnableEditMode, a Property<bool> each; save as Save; and its element's classList add and remove as Element.ClassList.Add and Remove; each EJ2 33.1.47's public member (@syncfusion/ej2-inplace-editor/src/inplace-editor/base/inplace-editor.d.ts:187, :320, :336, :587; @syncfusion/ej2-base/src/component.d.ts:17). EJ2's private disable and setFocus (inplace-editor.d.ts:541, :525) are declared by no door: Disabled disables and enables the editor, and EnableEditMode set true opens it and focuses its input unless beginEdit's cancelFocus is set (@syncfusion/ej2-inplace-editor/src/inplace-editor/base/inplace-editor.js:1319-1320, :799-803, :1046-1053) (M21.X402).

BeginEdit, EndEdit, Change, ActionBegin, ActionSuccess, SubmitClick and CancelClick hand payloads nested in FusionInPlaceEditor<TValue> under EJ2's names, BeginEditEventArgs, EndEditEventArgs, ChangeEventArgs, ActionBeginEventArgs, ActionEventArgs and, for the two clicks, MouseEvent, read with Read: beginEdit's cancel, cancelFocus and mode, and endEdit's action, cancel and mode, each optional as @syncfusion/ej2-inplace-editor/src/inplace-editor/base/interface.d.ts:86-107 marks it; change's Value and PreviousValue, the bound member's type; actionBegin's data, the submission's name, primaryKey and value, each text for every editor type (probe:ej2-inplaceeditor-action-begin-values), and its cancel, optional (:47-57); actionSuccess's data as Data<TResponse>() and its value (:58-68); and the name of each, which EJ2's observer sets on every payload it hands a listener (@syncfusion/ej2-base/src/observer.js:92, probe:ej2-payload-inplaceeditor-beginEdit, probe:ej2-payload-inplaceeditor-endEdit, probe:ej2-payload-inplaceeditor-change, probe:ej2-payload-inplaceeditor-actionBegin, probe:ej2-payload-inplaceeditor-actionSuccess, probe:ej2-payload-inplaceeditor-submitClick, probe:ej2-payload-inplaceeditor-cancelClick).

Html.InputField(plan, m => m.Member).FusionInPlaceEditor(build => ..) renders FusionInPlaceEditor<TProp> bound to the member, TProp its type, its starting value the member's value read through MVC with no compile and written by M21.D1 (D17.13, N17.10, M21.X403), and its input committed by EndEdit (M7.N3); the rendered editor's Reactive(e => e.Change, pipeline) handles its events from the plan's start, their payloads typed by the member, and pipeline.Component<FusionInPlaceEditor<DateTime?>>(id) reaches a date editor from any block.

features.oracle: Syncfusion EJ2 33.1.47's InPlaceEditor as its TypeScript declares it (@syncfusion/ej2-inplace-editor/src/inplace-editor/base/inplace-editor.d.ts, its payloads in @syncfusion/ej2-inplace-editor/src/inplace-editor/base/interface.d.ts, element in @syncfusion/ej2-base/src/component.d.ts), checked member by member by scratchpad m21/tools/dts.py with the slice's own package preferred and the element's classList by hand; enableEditMode's open and focus as inplace-editor.js runs them; main's registered value read as Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditorExtensions.cs:111-115 at 623dd4a27 writes it; and the browser, by spec/probes/ej2-payloads.mjs's thirteen InPlaceEditor facts, each payload's members and change's value for the Text, Numeric, Date, DateRange and MultiSelect editors (probe:ej2-payload-inplaceeditor-change, probe:ej2-inplaceeditor-change-Date and the rest).

defects.defect: Both lines call the editor's private disable and setFocus: main's Disable, Enable and Focus (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditorExtensions.cs:21, :25 at 623dd4a27) and the redesign's Disable and SetFocus (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditor.cs:23, :29 at 65fdf118d), which EJ2 declares private (@syncfusion/ej2-inplace-editor/src/inplace-editor/base/inplace-editor.d.ts:541, :525). The vendor contract analyzer (N17.2) refuses each by ALIS016 (X17.2); the rewrite declares EJ2's public disabled and enableEditMode (:320, :336) as Disabled and EnableEditMode, a Property<bool> each.

Both lines' render helper reads the bound member's starting value by compiling the view's expression and catching every exception it throws (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditorHtmlExtensions.cs:62, :68 at 623dd4a27; Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditor.cs:238, :244 at 65fdf118d): Expression.Compile is a run-time reflection call the reflection analyzer refuses in a shipped package outside validation, the one place D18.1 lists (N18.1, D18.4), and the catch hides an exception the member's getter throws. The rewrite reads the starting value through MVC with no compile, as every render helper does (D17.13, N17.10), and writes it by M21.D1.

Both lines read the editor's value and change's value and previousValue as string (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditorExtensions.cs:19, Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/Events/FusionInPlaceEditorChangeArgs.cs:11, :14 at 623dd4a27; Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditor.cs:19, :120, :123 at 65fdf118d), where EJ2 types the value string | number | Date | string[] | Date[] | number[] and change's string | string[] | number | number[] | boolean[] | Date | Date[] | DateRange (@syncfusion/ej2-inplace-editor/src/inplace-editor/base/inplace-editor.d.ts:187, @syncfusion/ej2-inplace-editor/src/inplace-editor/base/interface.d.ts:108), and each editor type hands its own kind: text for Text, a number for Numeric, a Date for Date, a list of two Dates for DateRange, not the DateRange object the TypeScript lists, and a list of the items' values for MultiSelect (probe:ej2-inplaceeditor-change-Text, probe:ej2-inplaceeditor-change-Numeric, probe:ej2-inplaceeditor-change-Date, probe:ej2-inplaceeditor-change-DateRange, probe:ej2-inplaceeditor-change-MultiSelect). A read of one kind fits no union of several, which ALIS037 refuses (D17.5). The rewrite's FusionInPlaceEditor<TValue> is generic over the bound member's type, which its render helper gives it, so Value, the input and change's Value and PreviousValue read the member's own type, as main reads the value by the member the field registers (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditorExtensions.cs:111-115 at 623dd4a27), and the vendor contract analyzer (N17.2) checks that type against one type the union holds (ALIS037) and, since EJ2 documents the value null until set (@syncfusion/ej2-inplace-editor/src/inplace-editor/base/inplace-editor.d.ts:184), holds it to a type whose read admits null (ALIS019, D17.5), so a string? or decimal? member binds and a decimal member is refused, where main's ComponentProperty<string> states the value with no null (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditorExtensions.cs:18-19 at 623dd4a27).

Both lines start the editor by compiling the view's expression against the model and handing EJ2 the object it reads, builder.Value(_value) (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditorHtmlExtensions.cs:62-63, :95 at 623dd4a27; Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditor.cs:238-239, :271 at 65fdf118d), a catch turning any failure into no start (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditorHtmlExtensions.cs:68-71 at 623dd4a27; Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionInPlaceEditor/FusionInPlaceEditor.cs:244-247 at 65fdf118d). The rewrite's render helper starts the editor at the member's value, written by M21.D1; a helper that drops it shows EJ2's emptyText, Empty (@syncfusion/ej2-inplace-editor/src/inplace-editor/base/inplace-editor.d.ts:230-232), though the member holds a value, against D17.13.

features.summary: FusionMaskedTextBox, both lines' FusionInputMask renamed to Fusion and EJ2's class name: one declaration of the Syncfusion MaskedTextBox by its JavaScript names, value, focusIn and change, each EJ2 33.1.47's public member; the payload of change; the input it is, its value committed by change; and the render helpers that render it bound to a model member. Main spreads the slice over six files whose events, writes and calls name members by strings over ComponentRef, a payload class with setters and a Reactive extension on the vendor's builder; the redesign declares it in one file, the shape the rewrite keeps, with its value typed nullable as EJ2 documents it and its change payload nested under EJ2's interface name.

sentences.text: The declaration takes EJ2's class name, FusionMaskedTextBox, Fusion and EJ2's MaskedTextBox (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/maskedtextbox/maskedtextbox/maskedtextbox.d.ts:16), the prefix keeping it apart from Syncfusion's own C# names beside it, as MaskedTextBoxBuilder in Syncfusion.EJ2.Inputs (the owner, 2026-11-09: "to avoid name collision"); both lines' FusionInputMask and its render helpers are renamed to it.

FusionMaskedTextBox declares Value as Property<string?>, since EJ2 documents it null until a value is set (M21.X609); FocusIn as a method; and Change as an event whose payload is the listener's first argument; each named as EJ2 33.1.47 names its public member.
FusionMaskedTextBox.MaskChangeEventArgs, EJ2's change payload, reads Value, the text without the mask's literals, and IsInteracted.
A FusionMaskedTextBox bound to a member is an input: its Value, committed by Change, is what a form sends and a check reads.
field.FusionMaskedTextBox() and field.FusionMaskedTextBox(build => ..) render the element under the field's id and binding name, starting at the member's value as M21.D1 writes it.

The rendered FusionMaskedTextBox's Reactive(m => m.Change, pipeline) handles its change from the plan's start; pipeline.Input(m => m.EmergencyPhone).Component<FusionMaskedTextBox>() reaches it in any block (N14.4).

features.summary: FusionKanban: one declaration of the Syncfusion Kanban by its JavaScript names, each named as EJ2 names it, its cards, columns, swimlanes, spinner and card dialog, each EJ2 33.1.47's public member; the payloads of its fourteen events, nested in the declaration under EJ2's names; the column and header data it writes and reads, a column's key typed by the key type of the cards (M21.X303); and the render helper that renders it with an element id the view gives and a plan. Main spreads the slice over seven files whose calls name members by strings over ComponentRef, payload classes with setters, extensions that take the pipeline, a builder of its own and a Reactive extension on it, and deletes a card by its key; the redesign declares it in one file, the shape the rewrite keeps, with the dialog's action typed as EJ2 reads it, a card deleted by its key again, and its data named as the vendor names it.

sentences.text: public Property<IEnumerable<TCard>> Cards<TCard>() where TCard : class => Property<IEnumerable<TCard>>("dataSource");

FusionKanban declares the EJ2 Kanban by its JavaScript names, each as EJ2 names it: dataSource as DataSource<TCard>(); getColumnData and getSwimlaneData as GetColumnData<TCard, TKey> and GetSwimlaneData<TCard>, which return cards; DataBind, AddCard, UpdateCard, DeleteCard, AddColumn<TKey>, DeleteColumn, ShowColumn<TKey>, HideColumn<TKey>, ShowSpinner, HideSpinner, OpenDialog and CloseDialog; each EJ2 33.1.47's public member, and each argument taking any source of its type.

DeleteCard<TCard>(Arg<TCard> cardData) takes a card, a list of cards or a card's key, text or a number, with no class constraint, as deleteCard takes string | number | Record | Record[] and finds a key by the board's headerField, so a response's card id deletes its card as main's DeleteCard(json, x => x.CardId) does (M21.X302).

OpenDialog takes FusionKanban.CurrentAction, EJ2's CurrentAction, Add, Edit or Delete, an enum that carries System.Text.Json's string enum converter, so the live form writes Add as openDialog's CurrentAction takes it, as main's OpenAddDialog and OpenEditDialog wrote it (M21.X301).
DataSource<TCard>().Set(source) and then DataBind() replace the board's cards from any source, the two steps main's SetDataSource wrote as one.

ActionBegin<TCard>(), ActionComplete<TCard>(), DataBinding<TCard>(), DataBound<TCard>(), CardClick<TCard>(), CardDoubleClick<TCard>(), QueryCellInfo<TKey>(), CardRendered<TCard>(), DragStart<TCard>(), Drag<TCard>(), DragStop<TCard>(), DialogOpen<TCard>(), DialogClose<TCard>() and DataSourceChanged<TCard>() hand payloads nested in FusionKanban under EJ2's names, FusionKanban.ActionEventArgs<TCard>, FusionKanban.ReturnType<TCard>, the payload of dataBinding and dataBound with its Result and Count (@syncfusion/ej2-kanban/src/kanban/base/type.d.ts:7-11), and FusionKanban.QueryCellInfoEventArgs<TKey> among them, read with Read, each payload's cancel its Property<bool>, and DataSourceChanged's endEdit and cancelEdit its methods.

FusionKanban.ColumnsModel<TKey>, the column AddColumn<TKey> writes, and FusionKanban.HeaderArgs<TKey>, each header QueryCellInfo<TKey>() hands, name each member by [JsonPropertyName] as ColumnsModel and HeaderArgs name it: headerText, keyField, allowToggle, isExpanded, textField and count; a column's key is TKey, the key type of the cards the board is rendered with, wherever the board takes or hands one, as a header hands a column's key as the app gave it, text or a number (probe:ej2-payload-kanban-queryCellInfo-text, probe:ej2-payload-kanban-queryCellInfo-number, @syncfusion/ej2-kanban/src/kanban/base/layout-render.js:140, :308) (M21.X303).

Html.FusionKanban(plan, id, build => ..) renders the board; its Reactive(k => k.CardClick<TCard>(), pipeline) and its other events handle it from the plan's start, and pipeline.Component<FusionKanban>(id) reaches it from any block.

defects.defect: The redesign's OpenDialog takes its action as Arg<string> (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionKanban/FusionKanban.cs:87 at 65fdf118d) where EJ2's openDialog takes CurrentAction, 'Add' | 'Edit' | 'Delete' (@syncfusion/ej2-kanban/src/kanban/base/type.d.ts:15), so a view compiles with any text, and the redesign's sandbox keeps the vendor's literal as a constant of its own (Alis.Reactive.SandboxApp/Areas/Sandbox/Models/Components/Fusion/Kanban/KanbanModel.cs:36 at 65fdf118d); main's OpenAddDialog and OpenEditDialog wrote Add and Edit themselves (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionKanban/FusionKanbanExtensions.cs:193, :200 at 623dd4a27). The rewrite's OpenDialog in M21.N26 takes FusionKanban.CurrentAction, an enum that carries System.Text.Json's string enum converter (X17.46).

The redesign's DeleteCard takes only a class (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionKanban/FusionKanban.cs:58 at 65fdf118d) where EJ2's deleteCard takes a card's key as string | number, a card or a list of cards (@syncfusion/ej2-kanban/src/kanban/base/kanban.d.ts:502) and finds a key by the board's headerField (@syncfusion/ej2-kanban/src/kanban/actions/crud.js:114-117), so the build refuses main's delete of a card by the number a response holds (Alis.Reactive.SandboxApp/Areas/Sandbox/Views/Components/Fusion/Kanban/Index.cshtml:109 at 623dd4a27). The rewrite's DeleteCard in M21.N26 takes a card, a list of cards or a card's key, text or a number, as deleteCard takes them, with no class constraint.

FusionKanbanColumn and FusionKanbanHeaderArgs carry no [JsonPropertyName] on either line (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionKanban/FusionKanbanExtensions.cs:216-222 at 623dd4a27; Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionKanban/FusionKanban.cs:254-264, :317-330 at 65fdf118d), while addColumn's ColumnsModel and QueryCellInfo's HeaderArgs name keyField, headerText, allowToggle, isExpanded, textField and count (@syncfusion/ej2-kanban/src/kanban/models/columns-model.d.ts:15-44, @syncfusion/ej2-kanban/src/kanban/base/interface.d.ts:177-184): the vendor contract analyzer's type check (N17.2) refuses each member by ALIS037 (X17.48), and the rewrite names each by [JsonPropertyName]. A column's key is string | number wherever the board takes or hands one (@syncfusion/ej2-kanban/src/kanban/models/columns-model.d.ts:15, @syncfusion/ej2-kanban/src/kanban/base/interface.d.ts:179, @syncfusion/ej2-kanban/src/kanban/base/kanban.d.ts:429, :527, :535), and a header hands it as the app gave it, text for a board of text keys and a number for one of number keys (probe:ej2-payload-kanban-queryCellInfo-text, probe:ej2-payload-kanban-queryCellInfo-number, @syncfusion/ej2-kanban/src/kanban/base/layout-render.js:140, :308), where the redesign reads and writes it as string (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionKanban/FusionKanban.cs:34, :71, :75, :257, :323 at 65fdf118d): a read of one kind fits no union of two, which ALIS037 refuses (D17.5). The rewrite types a column's key by TKey, the key type of the cards the board is rendered with, in ColumnsModel<TKey>, HeaderArgs<TKey> through QueryCellInfo<TKey>(), ShowColumn<TKey>, HideColumn<TKey> and GetColumnData<TCard, TKey>, and the analyzer checks TKey against one type the union holds.

Both lines render the Kanban by EJ2's own builder at the view's id and hand it to the view's build, html.EJS().Kanban(elementId) then build(builder) (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionKanban/FusionKanbanHtmlExtensions.cs:29-30 at 623dd4a27; Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionKanban/FusionKanban.cs:358-359 at 65fdf118d), so the options the view sets start it. A helper that renders before build, or at another id, draws no column and no card, EJ2's columns [] and dataSource [] (@syncfusion/ej2-kanban/src/kanban/base/kanban.d.ts:144-146, :109-112), and the plan's CardClick handler (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionKanban/FusionKanban.cs:113 at 65fdf118d; @syncfusion/ej2-kanban/src/kanban/base/kanban.d.ts:270) listens to no component, against D17.13.

features.summary: FusionSchedule: one declaration of the Syncfusion Schedule by its JavaScript names, its view, selected date, events through eventSettings, its editor, refresh, print and scroll, each EJ2 33.1.47's public member and named as EJ2 names it; the payloads of its nine events, nested in the declaration under EJ2's names, an event's data the app's own class; FusionSchedule.CurrentAction, EJ2's CurrentAction, the actions its methods take; the render helper that renders it with an element id the view gives and a plan; and the Fusion components of the partials a request loads beside it. Main spreads the slice over fifteen files whose calls name members by strings over ComponentRef, payload classes with setters, one app's event fields in a framework type, dates read as text, a builder of its own and a Reactive extension on it; the redesign declares it in one file, the shape the rewrite keeps, with its dates read as dates and its actions written as EJ2 reads them.

FusionSchedule declares the EJ2 Schedule by its JavaScript names, each as EJ2 names it: currentView and selectedDate as CurrentView and SelectedDate; eventSettings as EventSettings, a LiveObject<FusionSchedule.EventSettingsModel>(nullable: true), since EJ2 documents it null until set (@syncfusion/ej2-schedule/src/schedule/base/schedule.d.ts:705-707) and D17.5 declares nullable a live object such a member holds (M21.X307), whose dataSource is DataSource<TEvent>(); dataBind, getEvents, addEvent, saveEvent, deleteEvent, openEditor, closeEditor, refreshEvents, print, scrollTo, getCurrentViewDates, closeQuickInfoPopup and closeTooltip as DataBind, GetEvents, AddEvent, SaveEvent, DeleteEvent, OpenEditor, CloseEditor, RefreshEvents, Print, ScrollTo, GetCurrentViewDates, CloseQuickInfoPopup and CloseTooltip; each EJ2 33.1.47's public member, and each argument taking any source of its type.

FusionSchedule.CurrentAction, EJ2's CurrentAction, carries System.Text.Json's string enum converter, so the live form writes Save, DeleteOccurrence and the other actions as saveEvent, deleteEvent and openEditor's CurrentAction takes them (M21.X305, probe:ej2-schedule-save-event-action).

An event's data is the app's own class: GetEvents<TEvent>(), ActionBegin<TEvent>(), EventRendered<TEvent>() and PopupOpen<TEvent>() read it as TEvent; AddEvent, SaveEvent and OpenEditor take it from any source, and DeleteEvent<TKey> an event's key; EventSettings.DataSource<TEvent>().Set(source) and then DataBind() replace the events, the two steps main's SetDataSource wrote as one.

Navigating hands FusionSchedule.NavigatingEventArgs, which reads currentDate and previousDate as ReadOnly<DateTime>, so a text set from either shows its local day and a request sends it as offsetless text (M21.X306, probe:ej2-payload-schedule-navigating).

CellClick, EventClick, ActionBegin<TEvent>(), ActionComplete, Navigating, PopupOpen<TEvent>(), PopupClose, DataBound and EventRendered<TEvent>() hand payloads nested in FusionSchedule under EJ2's names, read with Read, each payload's cancel its Property<bool>.

A Fusion component in a partial that a request loads into a slot beside the schedule starts by the ScriptManager script the partial ends with, which the load runs after the content replaces the slot's and before the partial's plan starts (M9.D1); both lines run it so, main through EJ2's append and the redesign by replacing each script, and the plan each partial starts is module 9's.

Html.FusionSchedule(plan, id, build => ..) renders the schedule; its Reactive(c => c.Navigating, pipeline) and its other events handle it from the plan's start, and pipeline.Component<FusionSchedule>(id) reaches it from any block.

features.oracle: Syncfusion EJ2 33.1.47's Schedule as its TypeScript declares it (@syncfusion/ej2-schedule/src/schedule/base/schedule.d.ts, its event payloads in src/schedule/base/interface.d.ts, CurrentAction and View in src/schedule/base/type.d.ts, EventSettingsModel in src/schedule/models/event-settings-model.d.ts), each JavaScript name read there by hand, each event's payload interface to its closing brace with the interfaces it extends, scratchpad m21/tools/dts.py's flags taken as leads; the sandbox's edit partials on both lines; and the browser, by spec/probes/ej2-payloads.mjs (probe:ej2-payload-schedule-navigating, probe:ej2-schedule-save-event-action) and the promises.

defects.defect: The redesign's ScheduleAction carries no string converter (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionSchedule/FusionSchedule.cs:278 at 65fdf118d), which its own literal writer covers by writing an enum argument by its name (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Values/ValueExpression.cs:52 at 65fdf118d); in the live form (D7.7) saveEvent, deleteEvent and openEditor receive 1 for Save where CurrentAction is 'Add' | 'Save' | 'Delete' | 'DeleteOccurrence' | 'DeleteSeries' | 'EditOccurrence' | 'EditSeries' | 'EditFollowingEvents' | 'DeleteFollowingEvents' (@syncfusion/ej2-schedule/src/schedule/base/type.d.ts:36). The vendor contract analyzer's type check (N17.2) refuses the enum against the vendor's literal union by ALIS037 (X17.46), and the rewrite's FusionSchedule.CurrentAction carries System.Text.Json's string enum converter, as saveEvent saves an event given 'Save' and leaves it given 1 (probe:ej2-schedule-save-event-action). Main writes the action as text by hand (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionSchedule/FusionScheduleExtensions.cs:198, :203, :208 at 623dd4a27).

Main declares Navigating's currentDate and previousDate as text (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionSchedule/Events/FusionScheduleOnNavigating.cs:13, :16 at 623dd4a27) where EJ2 hands a Date (@syncfusion/ej2-schedule/src/schedule/base/interface.d.ts:194, :196), and main's text conversion writes a Date as its UTC instant (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/shared/shape-convert.ts:155 at 623dd4a27): a label set from either shows 2026-11-16T08:00:00.000Z in America/Los_Angeles where a date shown as text is its local day, 2026-11-16, and the request main's sandbox gathers currentDate into (Alis.Reactive.SandboxApp/Areas/Sandbox/Views/Components/Fusion/Schedule/Index.cshtml:291 at 623dd4a27) sends that instant where a DateTime goes with no offset. The redesign reads both as ReadOnly<DateTime> (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionSchedule/FusionSchedule.cs:203, :206 at 65fdf118d), which the rewrite keeps.

The redesign declares eventSettings as Object<FusionScheduleEventSettings>(), a live object with no null mark (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionSchedule/FusionSchedule.cs:35 at 65fdf118d), where EJ2 documents it null until set (@syncfusion/ej2-schedule/src/schedule/base/schedule.d.ts:705-707): the vendor contract analyzer (N17.2) reads a member documented @default null with null added to its type (D17.5), which a live object meets only declared nullable: true, and refuses the declaration by ALIS019. The rewrite's EventSettings is LiveObject<FusionSchedule.EventSettingsModel>(nullable: true). Main declares no door for eventSettings and writes its dataSource by a mapped path (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionSchedule/FusionScheduleExtensions.cs:62 at 623dd4a27).

features.summary: FusionSidebar: one declaration of the Syncfusion Sidebar by its JavaScript names, isOpen, show, hide, toggle, open and close, each EJ2 33.1.47's public member; the payload of open and close, nested under EJ2's interface name, with the Cancel EJ2 reads back, which neither line declares; and the render helper that renders it under the developer's id. sentences.text: FusionSidebar declares the EJ2 Sidebar by its JavaScript names: isOpen as IsOpen, a Property<bool>; show, hide and toggle as Show, Hide and Toggle; and open and close as Open and Close, whose payload is FusionSidebar.EventArgs; each EJ2 33.1.47's public member (@syncfusion/ej2-navigations/src/sidebar/sidebar.d.ts:106, :246, :238, :265, :202, :196). Open and Close carry main's Opened and Closed, which listen to the same two events.

FusionSidebar.EventArgs, EJ2's EventArgs nested under its name (@syncfusion/ej2-navigations/src/sidebar/sidebar.d.ts:316-337), reads IsInteracted, an optional ReadOnly<bool>, true when the user opened or closed the sidebar and false when a method did (@syncfusion/ej2-navigations/src/sidebar/sidebar.js:228, :293), and Cancel, an optional Property<bool> EJ2 reads back to keep the sidebar as it is (@syncfusion/ej2-navigations/src/sidebar/sidebar.js:232, :297), which neither line declares. It declares no member for model and element, the component and its element, nor for event, the DOM's event; it replaces the redesign's FusionSidebarTransitionArgs and main's.

Html.FusionSidebar(plan, elementId, build => ..) renders the sidebar under the id the developer chose on EJ2's SidebarBuilder, as both lines do, and returns the rendered component in place of main's FusionSidebarBuilder<TModel> and its Reactive extension; its Reactive(b => b.Close, pipeline) handles its events from the plan's start, and pipeline.Component<FusionSidebar>(elementId) reaches it from any block.

Main writes the component's construction and its request as a script in the view, which waits for DOMContentLoaded; the redesign moves both into its component code, the shape the rewrite keeps, and both lines send the request with no antiforgery token and read the text of any status.

sentences.text: return new HtmlString(RenderButton(elementId, options) + RenderInitializer(elementId, options));

FusionSmartPasteButton declares the EJ2 SmartPasteButton by its JavaScript names: disabled as Disabled, a Property<bool>, and click and focusIn as Click and FocusIn, each EJ2 33.1.47's public member, which the SmartPasteButton takes from its Button (@syncfusion/ej2-buttons/src/smart-paste-button/smart-paste-button.d.ts:16; @syncfusion/ej2-buttons/src/button/button.d.ts:64, :176, :184).

What crosses the AI boundary is EJ2's, and the framework's component code carries it whole (M21.D801): on a click, EJ2 reads the clipboard's text and the fields of the button's form and asks its aiAssistHandler with EJ2's ChatOptions (@syncfusion/ej2-buttons/src/smart-paste-button/smart-paste-button.d.ts:4-15; @syncfusion/ej2-buttons/src/smart-paste-button/smart-paste-button.js:112-123, :125); the component code sends that object as the JSON body of a POST to the endpoint the view names, and hands EJ2 the response's whole text, read once the body has arrived, never a stream (streaming is out of 1.0, an owner decision); EJ2 fills each field a line FIELD name^^^value names and leaves one answered NO_DATA (@syncfusion/ej2-buttons/src/smart-paste-button/smart-paste-button.js:128, :161, :182). The app's endpoint, not the framework, calls the model.

Html.FusionSmartPasteButton(elementId, options => ..) renders the button with its construction options in a data attribute and no script, as the redesign does, and the framework's component code builds the SmartPasteButton when the element mounts, so a button in a partial view loaded into a slot works as one in the page (M21.X804); main writes a script into the view, which views never carry. pipeline.Component<FusionSmartPasteButton>(elementId) reaches it from any block.

The AI request is an unsafe request to the page's origin, so it carries the app's antiforgery token (D9.22, M21.X803): the render helper writes the request token into the construction options from the host's own antiforgery, IAntiforgery.GetAndStoreTokens on net10 and AntiForgery.GetTokens on net48, as D9.22 writes the plan's, and the component code sends it in the header RequestVerificationToken, the one place a JSON body carries it, on a POST to the page's origin alone; net10's antiforgery reads that header, and on net48 the endpoint takes the framework's [ValidateAntiForgeryHeader].

A response whose status is outside 200 to 299, or a request the network refuses, hands EJ2 no text, so no field changes and no error page is read as an answer; both lines hand EJ2 the text of any status. An empty AiAssistEndpoint is refused where the view renders (M21.X805), since a button that asks no endpoint fills nothing.

meanings.meaning: A Smart Paste's AI boundary is a POST the framework's component code sends and one text it receives. It sends EJ2's ChatOptions (@syncfusion/ej2-buttons/src/smart-paste-button/smart-paste-button.d.ts:4-15), built by EJ2 from the form's fields and the clipboard's text (@syncfusion/ej2-buttons/src/smart-paste-button/smart-paste-button.js:112-123), as the request's JSON body, with Content-Type application/json and the page's antiforgery request token in the header RequestVerificationToken when the endpoint is on the page's origin (D9.22). It receives the response's whole text, awaited once the body has arrived, when the status is 200 to 299, and hands EJ2 an empty text otherwise, which EJ2 reads as no answer (@syncfusion/ej2-buttons/src/smart-paste-button/smart-paste-button.js:128); EJ2 alone parses the text into fields (@syncfusion/ej2-buttons/src/smart-paste-button/smart-paste-button.js:161). The endpoint is the app's own and calls the model the app chose; nothing streams in 1.0 (an owner decision), and no plan step runs inside the answer, since an answer the vendor awaits is no expression D17.12 takes.
